panels.description: Reads the `version` label of `switchyard_build_info`. Row 50 is new since the previous revision: `direct-openrouter-nemotron-3-ultra-free` was admitted by release `20261127T091816Z-aaf1bec88835acac-c635222b`, so rows 50-55 were renumbered and the table is no longer '54 of 54'.

Three planes, kept apart on purpose. **Model input / output / doc tools** are what the vendor documents for the model, not what this deployment has carried. **SW t/v/vid** is what the Switchyard *route* declares from this manifest; a declaration is an admission gate — it never proves the vendor supports the modality, and it never proves the wire carries it. **Transport** is the wire family's status: `cfg` configured but unproven, `ex` an official provider example exists, `?` unknown.

> A route whose declared vision is `N` is **not** evidence that the model cannot see images. It means that route has never admitted one. Gemini 3 Flash/3.1/3.5/3.6 document image, audio, video and PDF input; the owner and Stephen routes both currently declare `vision=false` because the carrier was never qualified, which is a Switchyard statement, not a Google one.

**Input letters** t text · i image · a audio · v video · p pdf, each `✓` documented, `~` partial/example only, `cfg` id live but modalities undocumented, `?` no cited source, `NO` documented unsupported, `—` not an API modality. **Transport** `chat:obs` means this deployment has served that model id in the retained routing log (2026-11-21T00:55Z..2026-11-25T15:08Z); `chat:cfg` means declared and loadable, never seen serving. A model id shared by two targets cannot be attributed to one of them from the log alone. `?` means no cited source establishes the fact (the reason is named in the Evidence column); it is not a negative claim — it is not a negative.

**What this release changes, and why it is not a routing change.** Two defects, both in how the server *states* what happened rather than in what it chooses.

*Settlement.* A provider reading records the gap to the pre-read watermark as `pending`; nothing is forgiven at that moment. A later reading at least `SETTLEMENT_DELAY` (120 s) after the reading that found the gap may reclaim only the units the provider has not since counted. Three corrections landed here: an **unwatermarked reading declares no claim** (it previously carried the old gap forward, which let one window's gap be reclaimed against a baseline it was never measured against); a settled gap is **discharged** — reclaimed once, and anything still missing is measured afresh against the new reading; and `release_uncharged_at` **shrinks `pending.amount`** by the units it releases, so one unit cannot be reclaimed twice. `spent` stays monotonic; reclaimed units live in `uncharged` and are removed by `charged_on()`, which every admission and watermark site uses.

*Provider reason.* One classifier, `classify_with_scope(status, body)`, is now the single reading of a refusal body. It supplies the log reason, the `CredentialBlockKind` and — through `LlmCallObservation` — the `reason`/`scope` that `AttemptTrace` writes into `routing.decisions.jsonl`. `ProviderScope` is `account` / `free_allowance` / `model` / `unknown`, taken only from a marker the provider publishes; an unstated scope stays `unknown` and no block is derived from it. The older `QuotaScope` reading in `run.rs` was deleted: a second reading of the same body is how a marker teaches one consumer a scope the others do not know about. No raw provider body is logged.

**Live evidence from the deployed process (measured, no synthetic probe).** At `2026-11-27T22:39:13Z`, route `smart-route` attempted `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, received `http_429` in 484 ms and recorded `reason=provider_throttled`, `scope=unknown`; it then served `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` in 1,435 ms, and that attempt's record carries **no** reason — a call that produced an answer has no refusal to name. At `22:39:46Z` the same route considered **12** candidates, dispatched all twelve including `nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free`, demoted three leaves on `daily_allowance_exhausted` (ernie, gemini-3.8-flash, gemini-4-hydrogen) and served `tencent/hy4-flash` in 3,436 ms. Across 79,686 attempt records in the log, exactly the refused attempts that reached the provider carry a reason; none of the served attempts does.

**Residual 400s, classified.** In five consecutive `smart-route` records `deepseek-flash` returned `http_400` and is now recorded as `provider_invalid_request` / `unknown` in about 470-560 ms, rather than being lumped into a local `invalid_request`. The chain recovered each time on `tencent/hy4-flash`. That is a provider-side refusal this deployment does not mask; it is reported, not fixed here.
